engagement_background.objective: Reduce Advantia Health’s cost base by creating $0.7-1.4 M in annual savings across key clinical and indirect spend categories, while instituting stronger procurement processes and controls to boost EBITDA and enterprise value for the PE owners.
engagement_background.scope_summary: Treya will run strategic sourcing and/or GPO/incumbent negotiations for 10 categories representing about $19 M of the $45 M total spend analysed. Categories include Employee Benefits (optional), IUDs, Diagnostic & Lab Services, Billing/RCM, Medical Supplies & Equipment, Telecom, Data Center/Cloud, Office Supplies and Electronic Payment Processing (TBD). Engagement also covers a review of procurement processes/controls; some sub-categories may be ruled un-addressable after deep-dives.
constraints_challenges: Limited strategic procurement resources and focus inside Advantia prior to the project
Spend and item-level data is incomplete and spread across two AP systems and P-cards, requiring line-item data collection from suppliers
Supplier and system fragmentation caused by recent acquisitions (Advantia Mid-Atlantic vs. Heartland) with little back-end integration
Decentralized, multi-site clinical operations create varied purchasing practices and potential stakeholder resistance to supplier changes
Six-month timeline with a moratorium on parallel client-led sourcing activity to avoid market confusion
Need to preserve sensitive incumbent supplier relationships, especially in clinical categories such as IUDs and lab services

procurement_environment.data_availability: AP transaction data from Advantia and Heartland plus YTD P-card data were available; centralized contract repository and detailed usage data were not.
procurement_environment.data_quality_notes: Multiple supplier naming conventions, limited commodity descriptions, gaps in historical usage; acquisitions not fully integrated, so spend had to be manually categorized and supplemented by supplier-provided data.
